changes: Validate actual OS lock/unlock while connected and during pending Connect, preserving the app process and retiring the old session.
Kill only the confirmed sample process while connected or negotiating; require the Server lease to reclaim its orphan and a fresh process/session to reconnect.
Hold admitted text/binary sends with a development-only native-worker gate; preserve the real 30-second deadline and use an early-release control.
Preserve Timeout in both the atomic native snapshot and fatal event, so Direct polling cannot turn an early snapshot into InternalError before event dispatch.
Wait for asynchronous OS resume before issuing an explicit foreground command.
The sample delays reconnect until activation is stable for half a second; another deactivate or background event cancels it. Both C++ and regenerated Blueprint flows use this policy.

cleanup.adb_reverse_cleanup_note: Only ports allocated by these probes were removed; unrelated baseline ports were preserved.

engine_checkout_note: Per-build revisions and existing checkout changes are recorded. This is local validation, not clean-host reproduction. No Engine source was edited for this task.
limitations: Physical iOS acceptance remains deferred; simulator lock behavior is not physical-device acceptance.
Forced termination uses SIGKILL of the sample process, not low-memory eviction or a physical device reboot. No graceful client teardown is claimed for killed processes.
Send-queue expiry uses an explicitly enabled development automation gate. Peers and channels are real, but native backpressure is held by the fixture.
Controlled local verified HTTPS and TURN/UDP only; Internet NAT, Wi-Fi/cellular handover and ICE restart remain open.
Package sizes describe Development bundles, not Shipping downloads or measured RTC size deltas.

repaired_attempts: Corrected the development gate to query native channel state with an empty payload while retaining admitted send bytes; final packages contain this correction.
Refreshed each project Editor metadata before cooking. Retried a cook after an unrelated UBT process prevented SDK validation from acquiring its mutex; no SDK check was bypassed.
Preserved an old audit directory and wrote the corrected Server audit to a fresh accepted directory.
Rejected a Galaxy run that woke before the requested quiet interval, and another that exposed the host unlock/foreground race; the driver now waits for asynchronous resume.
Three Galaxy cases passed before another app took the foreground after process restart. Their preliminary evidence is preserved; final acceptance uses fresh rebuilt packages.
The sandbox denied loopback sockets to four Python fixture tests; the authorized local-socket run passed.
A simulator lock attempt was rejected because macOS was locked and Device Hub could not perform the action.

The first simulator expiry attempt reported Timeout at 30 seconds but the sample queried a retired native peer before the public state callback. The corrected checker waits for that callback within its existing deadline bound.

Blueprint expiry then exposed a real production race: Direct snapshot polling reported NativeError before the queued timeout event. The native snapshot now preserves the error atomically, and both observation paths use it. Two deterministic Unreal tests and fresh packaged suites validate the final fix.

The lock runner allowed 90 seconds for owner unlock but reused a 60-second app-switch bound. Valid 62- and 75-second lock recoveries were rejected. Lock validation now uses the existing 120-second probe bound, with a regression test retaining callback/state checks; those rejected cases were rerun.

An otherwise successful simulator pending-Connect case exceeded the existing 60-second background interval because the UI driver lost its window target. It was excluded and rerun using the Home control.

Some simulator app launches stalled before creating a UIView. Those runs were rejected and their disposable simulators removed; fresh fixtures passed the termination checks. The startup-stall cause remains unconfirmed.

A pending-Connect simulator attempt exhausted its HTTP request retries while awaiting the manual lock action. That failed case was excluded and rerun promptly; its already-passed connected-lock case was retained.
Device Hub control calls intermittently timed out before fixture selection or lock verification. Unverified attempts were rejected and retained separately.

The simulator side button exposed a transient deactivate/reactivate/deactivate sequence during locking. Immediate sample reconnect started a second session before suspension. The sample now cancels a pending resume on deactivation and reconnects only after stable activation; both mobile profiles were rebuilt. Only verified passing cases from those packages are counted below.

The Galaxy switched to Recents, the sample was killed, and PR3 resumed during an Android impairment regression. That interrupted run is preserved; only passing cases from accepted runs are counted. No action was taken against unrelated apps.

Later Galaxy lock attempts exceeded the owner-unlock window; two retries woke before the required quiet interval, including an Android-recorded power-button wake. These attempts are rejected. The runner now prints a distinct quiet-interval completion marker before requesting test unlock, separate from cleanup unlock.
